_: The deployed DogTag system on ROAX. One set. Every address here was deployed by contracts/script/Deploy.s.sol in a single run, and every contract in contracts/src is represented exactly once. This file describes what is running, not how it came to be.
_roles: admin is the protocol authority: it owns ProviderRegistry (Ownable2Step) and holds DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE on DogTagSBTConsent, VerificationRegistryConsent and ProtocolRegistry, plus PUBLISHER_ROLE on the last. It is also the key that must broadcast Deploy.s.sol, because the registrar wiring in that script is onlyOwner on a core the script has just handed to it.
_custodian: The SBT's immutable neutral custodian. Every dog tag is minted here and never to an owner's wallet, so ownerOf carries no owner meaning and can never be compared as identity. It must have no code, hold no role anywhere, and never sign - it is a sink, not an actor.
_frozen_verifier: Groth16VerifierConsent is redeployed rather than reused, and its runtime bytecode is byte-identical to the previously deployed frozen-ceremony verifier - checked directly with cast code against the prior live verifier before and after the broadcast, and 1933 bytes in both. So the on-chain VK is unchanged and NO zero-knowledge artifact rotated: the consent circuit, its ceremony, consent_final.zkey (sha256 f83a111f...), consent.graph and both mobile bundles are untouched by this deployment. Changing any of them would be a ceremony decision, not a deployment one.
_root_index: VerificationRegistryConsent.rootIndex is the DogTagIssuerFactory. It is immutable, so the factory named here is the one this registry resolves every anchored root through for its whole life - replacing the factory means replacing the registry too, and repointing every client. That is the deliberate price of the pointer not being rewritable by anyone.
_publication: ProtocolRegistry carries NO published discovery set yet. Publishing is a separate, two-phase, timelocked operation - see contracts/script/PublishProtocolVersions.s.sol. Until it runs, an app validating a platform's version claim against this anchor resolves nothing and fails closed, which is the correct state for an unpublished deployment.
_deployment: 2026-08-03, ROAX chain 135. All nine contracts deployed by one run of contracts/script/Deploy.s.sol, broadcast by admin 0x8E27E117... at blocks 332371-332382 (12 transactions: 9 CREATEs then the 3 onlyOwner registrar-wiring calls). VERIFIED: every receipt status 0x1; all nine deployed runtimes compared against the compiled artifacts (Groth16VerifierConsent, DogTagIssuer and ProviderRegistry byte-for-byte EXACT, the other six exact once their immutable slots are blanked on both sides); and every immutable read back from the chain - vr.rootIndex/providerRegistry/sbt/zkVerifier, factory.registry/implementation, core.owner, sbt.custodian, domainResolver.factory, directory.core - each equal to the address deployed for it. The whole sequence was rehearsed first on an anvil fork of ROAX and produced identical addresses.
_provisioning: Deployed and wired, with NO provider onboarded: providerCount is 0, so no clone exists and nothing has been issued. Registering a provider, clearing it for a record type, attaching its clone and granting an issuance capability are registrar KYC decisions about a particular business, deliberately outside the deploy script - drive them from the admin portal's registrar surface.
